record.paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
record.original_question: Let f: C^2 -> C^2 be an entire holomorphic mapping. Must the Euclidean volume of the image f(C^2), measured in the usual Euclidean volume on C^2, be infinite?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Equip $\mathbb{C}^2$ with its standard Euclidean (Lebesgue) volume, identifying $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $\mathbb{R}^4$. Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2$ be an entire holomorphic mapping, i.e. a map $f(z_1,z_2)=(f_1(z_1,z_2),f_2(z_1,z_2))$ whose components are entire holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{C}^2$. Consider the image set $f(\mathbb{C}^2)\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ and its 4-dimensional Lebesgue (Euclidean) measure $\mathrm{vol}\bigl(f(\mathbb{C}^2)\bigr)$. Must $\mathrm{vol}\bigl(f(\mathbb{C}^2)\bigr) = \infty$ for every such $f$? Equivalently, does there exist an entire holomorphic mapping $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ whose image has finite Euclidean volume?
artifact.category_tag: Several complex variables / entire holomorphic mappings
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a resolution of this question. It is consistent with the literature on holomorphic mappings $\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}^n$ (e.g. Rosay–Rudin and subsequent work), where many natural questions about the image of such mappings remain unresolved. No source found that proves the Euclidean volume of $f(\mathbb{C}^2)$ must be infinite, nor one that exhibits an entire $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ with finite-volume image.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic Maps from C^n to C^n (Rosay–Rudin)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical paper on entire holomorphic mappings of C^n; many questions about images remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference indicating that image-related questions for entire maps C^n -> C^n are typically subtle and several remain open.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic Maps with Large Images
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of holomorphic maps with large/dense images in C^m, with controlled growth.
status_evidence.claim: Related results address density and size of images, but do not settle whether every entire map C^2 -> C^2 has infinite-volume image.
